sample_posts.text: 🇲🇦🇪🇸🔴⬛️Meta and TikTok have agreed to fact-check content on border crossings into Spain following a massive rush to enter Ceuta from Morocco, which resulted in almost 100 dead. This initiative aims to prevent criminal networks from misleading potential migrants with false information. An “ad-hoc escalation and cooperation mechanism with fact-checkers” has been established as part of crisis protocols, with daily discussions between the EU Commission, Europol, and the two companies. EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen also discussed the issue with Spanish digital economy minister Oscar Lopez. The viral videos that encouraged the crossing were intended to highlight migration pressures.
